markdown_report:
At 20% progress, select a controlled terminal-supervision allocation experiment with explicit provenance. The supplied diagnostics support investigating training–inference alignment, but establish neither an HR@10 improvement nor an optimal probability.

Three starting insights guide the experiment. First, Electronics has a 5.71% negative-wins rate versus 2.07% for Movies_and_TV. These training margins identify different discrimination regimes but cannot establish validation ranking quality. Second, appended-MASK user RankMe is approximately 24 in Electronics and Industrial_and_Scientific, while item RankMe is approximately 49. This motivates monitoring representation geometry without diagnosing collapse. Third, training allocation is null across categories. Diagnostic terminal coverage near 20% cannot identify branch probabilities, and the supplied definitions warn that earlier changes also altered prefix context.

Three literature insights constrain interpretation. BERT4Rec [1] establishes masked-item learning and terminal prediction. It motivates studying supervision allocation without establishing that 0.75 is preferable. PyTorch’s loss definition [2] makes normalization part of the objective. Separately normalized branch means can preserve equal branch coefficients despite unequal example counts. Sampling research [3] distinguishes sampled evaluation from broader ranking behavior. Consequently, simulator feedback and training margins remain explanatory observations alongside the pinned selection metric.

The framework separates three directions:

| Direction | Controlled component | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| Supervision alignment | Terminal versus random allocation [1] | Context and normalization confounding |
| Optimization accounting | Actual loss coefficients [2] | Coefficients do not identify gradient influence |
| Behavioral sensitivity | Frozen history perturbations | Sensitivity does not establish current intent |

Three atomic ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Prespecified p=0.75 allocation with preserved context [1,2] | 3/6/3 | Minimal, interpretable intervention | Existing technique; probability lacks empirical justification |
| Sparse branch-gradient accounting [2] | 4/6/5 | Measures local optimization interaction | Extra compute; conflict need not harm ranking |
| Matched recent/random deletion probe [3] | 3/5/3 | Tests reliance on recent history | Diagnostic only; cannot infer unresolved needs |

Choose the first idea. Preserve the corrected baseline’s prefix/window construction, random corruption, architecture, optimizer, and exact loss reduction; change only allocation where the sampler supports this comparison. If the baseline constructs distinct paired views, preserve those view generators and describe the change as allocation between those views. Never replace sampled prefixes with latest-history windows and claim a probability-only effect.

Record explicit branch IDs, target counts, loss sums, denominators, coefficients, and empty branches during training; persist summaries with the selected checkpoint. Train one BERT4Rec per category and select using unchanged host validation macro HR@10. Keep appended-MASK inference and the maximum-nonpadding readout. No validation results are supplied, so effectiveness remains untested.

References: [1] BERT4Rec, arXiv:1904.06690. [2] PyTorch CrossEntropyLoss documentation. [3] On the Reliability of Sampling Strategies, RecSys 2025.

idea.description: Prespecify terminal-only supervision probability p=0.75 per example while preserving the corrected BERT4Rec baseline’s context generators, random corruption procedure, and exact loss reduction. Train one independent model per category and persist explicit allocation accounting.
idea.motivation: Terminal-only masking matches appended-MASK prediction structurally. However, unavailable training allocation and documented context confounding prevent attributing earlier behavior to branch probability. At 20% progress, a small, prespecified intervention with faithful accounting is more defensible than adding architectural complexity. The supplied margins and geometry are diagnostic observations, not evidence that this intervention improves HR@10.
idea.implementation_notes: Apply the intervention to the supplied corrected baseline rather than inventing its missing implementation. Preserve Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl routing; DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; preprocessing seed 0; training seed 42; single-GPU execution; at most 200 epochs; and 200 batches per epoch. Keep artifacts beneath the trial directory. Preserve baseline user/prefix endpoint sampling, truncation, positional IDs, corruption rules, optimizer, loss coefficients, empty-branch policy, and checkpoint-selection rule. If the baseline uses distinct paired terminal and reconstruction views, retain their respective context generators; do not claim a shared-window probability-only comparison unless that equivalence is established. With separate branch means, preserve their actual coefficients: p=0.75 changes sample allocation and estimator variance, not necessarily objective weight. Log explicit branch counts, valid-target counts, detached CE sums, exact denominators, coefficients, objective contributions, and empty/skipped counts; save summaries so diagnosis remains available after checkpoint loading. Preserve the reserved MASK token and masked-target supervision without shifted-target leakage. At inference keep at most L-1 history items, append MASK, left-pad, and select the maximum nonpadding index. Keep the predictor writer consistent with the checkpoint and architecture. Preserve sample_batch, ModelView.model, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, and review_data. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Diagnostic batches remain (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B x L tensors. Use only supplied histories, timestamps, titles, and descriptions; unavailable metadata and traits remain unavailable. Host selection remains the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10; do not modify candidates, splits, or evaluator. Each category loads exactly one trained checkpoint, without averaging or score fusion.
idea.pseudocode:
for category in FOUR_CATEGORIES:
    baseline = initialize_corrected_bert4rec(category, seed=42)
    record_baseline_context_generators_and_loss_semantics(baseline)
    for epoch in baseline_epoch_schedule(max_epochs=200):
        for step in range(200):
            branches = baseline_seeded_branch_draws(p_terminal=0.75)
            # Preserve each baseline branch's original user/prefix/window generator.
            batch, provenance = baseline_construct_views(branches)
            # Terminal views replace their final nonpadding target with reserved MASK.
            # Random views retain the supplied random-mask procedure and fallback.
            outputs = baseline.model(batch.sequence)
            loss, detached_accounting = exact_baseline_loss_with_accounting(
                outputs, batch.labels, provenance
            )
            # Preserve original denominators, coefficients, and empty-branch handling.
            baseline.optimizer_step(loss)
            persist_training_counters(detached_accounting, provenance)
        baseline_checkpoint_selection_using_unchanged_validation_rule()
    save_one_selected_checkpoint_with_configuration_and_allocation_summary()
    write_matching_category_predictor()

predict(history, candidates):
    sequence = baseline_left_pad(history[-(L-1):] + [MASK])
    features = model.log2feats(sequence)
    j = max_index_where(sequence != PAD)
    return model.predict_score(features[j], candidates)

# Host independently evaluates unchanged validation candidates and macro HR@10.
# No executable baseline replacement is specified because its source is absent.

originality.positive: Explicitly separating example allocation, context generation, and loss coefficients makes the intervention scientifically interpretable.
originality.negative: Terminal masking already belongs to BERT4Rec; p=0.75 is a prespecified hyperparameter hypothesis rather than a new modeling principle.

future_potential.positive: Reliable provenance could support later studies of context alignment, estimator variance, and supervision influence within one network.
future_potential.negative: Allocation alone may not resolve the specific compatibility, redundancy, and current-purpose failures in simulator feedback.

code_difficulty.positive: The intended model change is restricted to sampler allocation and leaves inference architecture intact.
code_difficulty.negative: Faithful implementation requires the absent baseline source and careful preservation of paired-view construction, reduction semantics, and persisted diagnostics.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Establishes bidirectional masked-item learning for sequential recommendation.
Provides the methodological basis for retaining Cloze supervision and terminal MASK prediction.
limitations: Does not establish p=0.75 as optimal for the supplied corrected baseline.
Does not recover this trial’s missing sampler provenance or demonstrate its validation performance.

related_work.title: PyTorch CrossEntropyLoss documentation
contributions: Specifies ignored-target handling and mean-reduction denominators.
Supports exact accounting of pooled versus separately normalized branch objectives.
limitations: Documents loss semantics rather than recommendation effectiveness.
Loss coefficients and target counts alone do not determine gradient influence.

related_work.title: On the Reliability of Sampling Strategies
contributions: The supplied search summary reports that candidate sampling affects model comparisons and agreement with full evaluation.
Motivates separating pinned sampled-candidate validation from full-catalog simulator observations.
limitations: Does not justify changing the host’s fixed evaluator.
Does not establish that healthy training margins imply strong validation HR@10 for these models.
